15// The current tolerance is set to 0.25. Since `sqrt` doesn't work in const contexts, we instead
16// hardcode the squared tolerance and derive the others from that.
17pub(crate) const SQRT_TOL: f64 = 0.5;
18pub(crate) const TOL: f64 = SQRT_TOL * SQRT_TOL;
19pub(crate) const TOL_2: f64 = TOL * TOL;

21/// A point.
22#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq)]
23pub struct Point {
24    /// The x coordinate of the point.
25    pub x: f32,
26    /// The y coordinate of the point.
27    pub y: f32,
28}
29
30impl Point {
31    /// The point `(0, 0)`.
32    pub const ZERO: Self = Self::new(0., 0.);
33
34    /// Create a new point.
35    pub const fn new(x: f32, y: f32) -> Self {
36        Self { x, y }
37    }
38}
39
40impl From<kurbo::Point> for Point {
41    #[inline(always)]
42    fn from(value: kurbo::Point) -> Self {
43        Self { x: value.x as f32, y: value.y as f32 }
44    }
45}
46
47impl core::ops::Add for Point {
48    type Output = Self;
49
50    fn add(self, rhs: Self) -> Self {
51        Self::new(self.x + rhs.x, self.y + rhs.y)
52    }
53}
54
55impl core::ops::Sub for Point {
56    type Output = Self;
57
58    fn sub(self, rhs: Self) -> Self {
59        Self::new(self.x - rhs.x, self.y - rhs.y)
60    }
61}
62
63impl core::ops::Mul<f32> for Point {
64    type Output = Self;
65
66    fn mul(self, rhs: f32) -> Self {
67        Self::new(self.x * rhs, self.y * rhs)
68    }
69}

87/// Flatten a filled Bézier path into line segments.
88///
89/// # Open subpaths and culling
90///
91/// Open subpaths in the input path get closed by connecting the last endpoint in the subpath to
92/// the starting point. The output lines in `line_buf` describe the flattened path, but these lines
93/// may describe open subpaths, as some path elements may have been culled.
94///
95/// For example, consider the following, where the box describes the viewport, a path is marked by
96/// `*`, and the region to be filled in the viewport is shaded. For ease of drawing the ASCII art,
97/// the path elements are all lines ([`PathEl::LineTo`]), but the same also holds for Bézier path
98/// elements.
99///
100/// ```text
101///    ---> winding scan direction
102///
103///                   * * * * *
104///                 *         *
105///    ---------- * -----     *
106///    |        *░░░░░░░|     *
107///    |      *░░░░░░░░░|     *
108///    |    *░░░░░░░░░░░|     *
109///    |  *░░░░░░░░░░░░░|     *
110///    |*░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░|     *
111///   *|░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░|     *
112/// *  |░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░|     *
113/// *  |░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░|     *
114/// *  ------------------     *
115/// *                         *
116/// *                         *
117/// *                         *
118/// *                         *
119/// *                         *
120/// *                         *
121/// *                         *
122/// * * * * * * * * * * * * * *
123/// ```
124///
125/// Because the winding scan direction is from left to right, only the left-of-viewport and
126/// diagonal lines matter in later stages of rendering for the winding number and pixel coverage.
127/// The other three lines can be culled.
128///
129/// ```text
130///                   *
131///                 *
132///    ---------- * -----
133///    |        *░░░░░░░|
134///    |      *░░░░░░░░░|
135///    |    *░░░░░░░░░░░|
136///    |  *░░░░░░░░░░░░░|
137///    |*░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░|
138///   *|░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░|
139/// *  |░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░|
140/// *  |░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░|
141/// *  ------------------
142/// *
143/// *
144/// *
145/// *
146/// *
147/// *
148/// *
149/// ```
150///
151/// It is important to keep these flattened subpaths open after culling, as closing the subpaths
152/// might yield different geometry like the following.
153///
154/// ```text
155///                   *
156///                 **
157///    ---------- * *----
158///    |        *░░*    |
159///    |      *░░░*     |
160///    |    *░░░░*      |
161///    |  *░░░░░*       |
162///    |*░░░░░░*        |
163///   *|░░░░░░*         |
164/// *  |░░░░░*          |
165/// *  |░░░░*           |
166/// *  --- * ------------
167/// *     *
168/// *    *
169/// *   *
170/// *  *
171/// * *
172/// **
173/// *
174/// ```
175pub fn fill(
176    level: Level,
177    path: impl IntoIterator<Item = PathEl>,
178    affine: Affine,
179    line_buf: &mut Vec<Line>,
180    ctx: &mut FlattenCtx,
181    cull_bbox: RectU16,
182) {
183    dispatch!(level, simd => fill_impl(simd, path, affine, line_buf, ctx, cull_bbox));
184}
185
186/// Flatten a filled bezier path into line segments.
187///
188/// See the note about open subpaths and culling on [`fill`].
189#[inline(always)]
190pub fn fill_impl<S: Simd>(
191    simd: S,
192    path: impl IntoIterator<Item = PathEl>,
193    affine: Affine,
194    line_buf: &mut Vec<Line>,
195    flatten_ctx: &mut FlattenCtx,
196    cull_bbox: RectU16,
197) {
198    line_buf.clear();
199    let mut lb = FlattenerCallback { line_buf, start: Point::ZERO, p0: Point::ZERO, is_nan: false };
200
201    crate::third_party::vello_common::flatten_simd::flatten(simd, path, affine, &mut lb, flatten_ctx, cull_bbox);
202
203    // A path that contains NaN is ill-defined, so ignore it.
204    if lb.is_nan {
205        warn!("A path contains NaN, ignoring it.");
206
207        line_buf.clear();
208    }
209}
210/// Flatten a stroked Bézier path into line segments.
211///
212/// See the note about open subpaths and culling on [`fill`].
213pub fn stroke(
214    level: Level,
215    // PdfCraft patch: `Clone` so the path can be stroked a second time.
216    path: impl IntoIterator<Item = PathEl> + Clone,
217    style: &Stroke,
218    affine: Affine,
219    line_buf: &mut Vec<Line>,
220    flatten_ctx: &mut FlattenCtx,
221    stroke_ctx: &mut StrokeCtx,
222    cull_bbox: RectU16,
223) {
224    // TODO: Temporary hack to ensure that strokes are scaled properly by the transform.
225    let tolerance = TOL / affine.as_coeffs()[0].abs().max(affine.as_coeffs()[3].abs()).max(1.);
226
227    expand_stroke(path.clone(), style, tolerance, stroke_ctx);
228    // PdfCraft patch: kurbo's stroker can put NaN into the outline of a curve that is nearly a
229    // line (all control points within a rounding error of the chord), and `fill` then drops the
230    // whole outline. Stroke it again with such curves as lines. A finite outline is unchanged.
231    // PdfCraft patch (4): it can also put NaN into the offset of a cubic whose second control
232    // point is its end point (as `y` builds), so that control point is moved off it in the same
233    // pass.
234    if !stroke_ctx.output().is_finite() {
235        let path = robust_for_stroking(path, tolerance);
236        expand_stroke(&path, style, tolerance, stroke_ctx);
237    }
238    fill(level, stroke_ctx.output(), affine, line_buf, flatten_ctx, cull_bbox);
239}
240
241// PdfCraft patch.
242/// `path` with each quadratic or cubic whose control points all lie within
243/// `tolerance` of its chord replaced by a line to its end point, and (patch (4)) each other
244/// cubic whose second control point is its end point given a short end handle instead
245/// ([`open_zero_end_handle`]). One element out per element in.
246fn robust_for_stroking(path: impl IntoIterator<Item = PathEl>, tolerance: f64) -> BezPath {
247    let mut out = BezPath::new();
248    let mut start = kurbo::Point::ZERO;
249    let mut last = start;
250    for el in path {
251        let el = match el {
252            PathEl::QuadTo(p1, p2) if near_segment(p1, last, p2, tolerance) => PathEl::LineTo(p2),
253            PathEl::CurveTo(p1, p2, p3) if near_segment(p1, last, p3, tolerance) && near_segment(p2, last, p3, tolerance) => PathEl::LineTo(p3),
254            PathEl::CurveTo(p1, p2, p3) => PathEl::CurveTo(p1, open_zero_end_handle(last, p1, p2, p3, tolerance), p3),
255            el => el,
256        };
257        match el {
258            PathEl::MoveTo(p) => {
259                start = p;
260                last = p;
261            }
262            PathEl::LineTo(p) | PathEl::QuadTo(_, p) | PathEl::CurveTo(_, _, p) => last = p,
263            PathEl::ClosePath => last = start,
264        }
265        out.push(el);
266    }
267    out
268}
269
270// PdfCraft patch (4).
271/// The second control point of the cubic `p0 p1 p2 p3`, moved `tolerance` towards `p1` (or `p0`
272/// when `p1` is that close too) when it sits on the end point `p3`, as a `y` curve's does.
273///
274/// There the curve's derivative vanishes at its end. kurbo finds the cusps of a wide stroke's
275/// offset curve with a root search on the curvature, which grows without bound towards such an
276/// end; at some widths the search returns the end point itself, and the unit tangent kurbo takes
277/// there is `0 / 0`. Only an exact zero does this: a handle even 1e-9 long strokes finitely, as
278/// does a first control point on the start point (`v`). The moved control point moves the curve
279/// by at most `4 / 9 * tolerance`.
280fn open_zero_end_handle(p0: kurbo::Point, p1: kurbo::Point, p2: kurbo::Point, p3: kurbo::Point, tolerance: f64) -> kurbo::Point {
281    if p2 != p3 {
282        return p2;
283    }
284    [p1, p0].into_iter().map(|q| q - p3).find(|v| v.hypot() > tolerance).map_or(p2, |v| p3 + v * (tolerance / v.hypot()))
285}
286
287/// Whether `p` is within `tolerance` of the segment from `a` to `b`. False for non-finite input.
288fn near_segment(p: kurbo::Point, a: kurbo::Point, b: kurbo::Point, tolerance: f64) -> bool {
289    let ab = b - a;
290    let len2 = ab.hypot2();
291    let t = if len2 > 0.0 { ((p - a).dot(ab) / len2).clamp(0.0, 1.0) } else { 0.0 };
292    (p - (a + ab * t)).hypot() <= tolerance
293}
294
295/// Expand a stroked path to a filled path.
296pub fn expand_stroke(path: impl IntoIterator<Item = PathEl>, style: &Stroke, tolerance: f64, stroke_ctx: &mut StrokeCtx) {
297    kurbo::stroke_with(path, style, &StrokeOpts::default(), tolerance, stroke_ctx);
298}
299
300struct FlattenerCallback<'a> {
301    line_buf: &'a mut Vec<Line>,
302    start: Point,
303    p0: Point,
304    is_nan: bool,
305}
306
307impl Callback for FlattenerCallback<'_> {
308    #[inline(always)]
309    fn callback(&mut self, el: LinePathEl) {
310        match el {
311            LinePathEl::MoveTo(p) => {
312                self.is_nan |= p.is_nan();
313
314                let p = p.into();
315                self.start = p;
316                self.p0 = p;
317            }
318            LinePathEl::LineTo(p) => {
319                self.is_nan |= p.is_nan();
320
321                let p = p.into();
322                self.line_buf.push(Line::new(self.p0, p));
323                self.p0 = p;
324            }
325        }
326    }
327}

329#[cfg(any())]
330mod tests {
331    use super::{FlattenCtx, Line, TOL, expand_stroke, stroke};
332    use crate::third_party::vello_common::geometry::RectU16;
333    use crate::third_party::vello_common::kurbo::{Affine, BezPath, Point, Stroke, StrokeCtx};
334    use alloc::vec::Vec;
335    use fearless_simd::Level;
336
337    fn stroke_lines(path: &BezPath, width: f64, ctx: &mut StrokeCtx) -> Vec<Line> {
338        let mut lines = Vec::new();
339        stroke(
340            Level::baseline(),
341            path,
342            &Stroke::new(width),
343            Affine::IDENTITY,
344            &mut lines,
345            &mut FlattenCtx::default(),
346            ctx,
347            RectU16::new(0, 0, 200, 200),
348        );
349        lines
350    }
351
352    // An outline in an Illustrator file (#4907) has a cubic whose control points are all equal
353    // and 0.001 from its start. kurbo's stroker gives that curve a NaN join, which made the whole
354    // outline disappear. The trigger depends on these exact coordinates.
355    #[cfg(any())]
356    fn a_tiny_degenerate_cubic_does_not_drop_the_stroke() {
357        let mut path = BezPath::new();
358        path.move_to((0.0, 0.0));
359        path.line_to((73.763, -0.536));
360        let p = Point::new(73.764, -0.536);
361        path.curve_to(p, p, p);
362
363        let mut ctx = StrokeCtx::default();
364        let lines = stroke_lines(&path, 0.34, &mut ctx);
365        assert!(!lines.is_empty(), "the stroke was dropped");
366        assert!(ctx.output().is_finite());
367        let max_x = lines.iter().map(|l| l.p0.x.max(l.p1.x)).fold(f32::MIN, f32::max);
368        assert!(max_x > 73.0, "the stroke ends at x = {max_x}");
369    }
370
371    #[cfg(any())]
372    fn a_path_with_nan_is_still_dropped() {
373        let mut path = BezPath::new();
374        path.move_to((10.0, 10.0));
375        path.curve_to((f64::NAN, 10.0), (10.0, 60.0), (60.0, 60.0));
376        let lines = stroke_lines(&path, 2.0, &mut StrokeCtx::default());
377        assert!(lines.is_empty());
378    }
379
380    /// The outline of `path` stroked with `style`, drawn translated by (80, -136) so that the
381    /// test paths below land inside the 200 × 200 cull box, and whether kurbo's outline was finite.
382    fn stroke_style_lines(path: &BezPath, style: &Stroke) -> (Vec<Line>, bool) {
383        let mut lines = Vec::new();
384        let mut ctx = StrokeCtx::default();
385        stroke(
386            Level::baseline(),
387            path,
388            style,
389            Affine::translate((80.0, -136.0)),
390            &mut lines,
391            &mut FlattenCtx::default(),
392            &mut ctx,
393            RectU16::new(0, 0, 200, 200),
394        );
395        let finite = ctx.output().is_finite();
396        (lines, finite)
397    }
398
399    // A file in the PDFBox issue tracker strokes "XX" outlines at 32 pt whose subpaths include
400    // `y` curves (the second control point on the end point, so the end tangent vanishes), and at
401    // 16, 32 and 63 pt kurbo's offset of one of them came back with NaN, so the whole outline was
402    // dropped. These exact coordinates are the trigger. `v` (the first control point on the start
403    // point) is the mirrored case, the same two curves run backwards; kurbo strokes it finitely,
404    // and it is checked as a guard.
405    #[cfg(any())]
406    fn a_wide_stroke_of_a_curve_with_a_zero_end_tangent_is_drawn() {
407        use crate::third_party::vello_common::kurbo::{Cap, Join};
408        let a = Point::new(21.4166, 234.5928);
409        let b = Point::new(18.9478, 236.3428);
410        let e = Point::new(20.8697, 238.4209);
411        let mut y = BezPath::new();
412        y.move_to(a);
413        y.curve_to(Point::new(19.9009, 236.0303), b, b);
414        y.curve_to(Point::new(19.2603, 238.4209), e, e);
415        let mut v = BezPath::new();
416        v.move_to(e);
417        v.curve_to(e, Point::new(19.2603, 238.4209), b);
418        v.curve_to(b, Point::new(19.9009, 236.0303), a);
419
420        let mut failures = Vec::new();
421        for (name, path) in [("y", &y), ("v", &v)] {
422            for width in 1..=64 {
423                for join in [Join::Miter, Join::Round, Join::Bevel] {
424                    for cap in [Cap::Butt, Cap::Round, Cap::Square] {
425                        let style = Stroke::new(f64::from(width)).with_join(join).with_caps(cap);
426                        let (lines, finite) = stroke_style_lines(path, &style);
427                        if lines.is_empty() || !finite {
428                            failures.push((name, width, join, cap));
429                        }
430                    }
431                }
432            }
433        }
434        assert!(failures.is_empty(), "strokes dropped: {failures:?}");
435    }
436
437    // A regression guard: it passes with or without the patch.
438    #[cfg(any())]
439    fn a_finite_outline_is_stroked_as_before() {
440        let mut path = BezPath::new();
441        path.move_to((10.0, 10.0));
442        path.curve_to((60.0, 10.0), (10.0, 60.0), (60.0, 60.0));
443        let style = Stroke::new(2.0);
444        let mut expected = StrokeCtx::default();
445        expand_stroke(&path, &style, TOL, &mut expected);
446
447        let mut ctx = StrokeCtx::default();
448        let lines = stroke_lines(&path, 2.0, &mut ctx);
449        assert!(!lines.is_empty());
450        assert_eq!(ctx.output(), expected.output());
451    }
452}
